nodes.label: Testing strategy
nodes.rationale: Table-driven unit tests with no mocking framework (interfaces where stubs are required, concrete types where not); integration tests run against a real DB via TEST_DATABASE_URL with migrations in setup; handler tests use the real chi router and middleware; shared helpers in internal/testutil.

nodes.label: chi HTTP router
nodes.rationale: Chosen for net/http compatibility, clean route groups, and the whole stdlib ecosystem.

nodes.label: cobra CLI framework
nodes.rationale: Industry standard, subcommand nesting, built-in help.

nodes.label: Config management (env + .env)
nodes.rationale: Standard 12-factor pattern; loading order flags > environment variables > .env file; .env is ignored in production.

nodes.label: go-playground/validator
nodes.rationale: Struct-tag validation, standard in Go.

nodes.label: GoBase template
nodes.rationale: Batteries-included Go project template inspired by Laravel's artisan: one binary with subcommands (serve, migrate, jwt), chi HTTP API, sqlx DB access, golang-migrate, HMAC JWT, slog. Clone, run ./setup.sh, start building.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256 JWT authentication
nodes.rationale: Simple shared secret, stateless verification; ParseToken validates signature AND expiry; middleware injects Claims into request context.

nodes.label: setup.sh bootstrap script
nodes.rationale: Interactive bootstrap: prompts for new module path, replaces github.com/wesleysnt/gobase across all .go files and go.mod, copies .env.example to .env, runs go mod tidy.

nodes.label: slog structured logging
nodes.rationale: Stdlib structured logging; JSON format in production, text format in development.

nodes.label: sqlx database layer
nodes.rationale: Raw SQL with struct scanning, minimal magic.

nodes.label: user domain module (reference slice)
nodes.rationale: Fully working CRUD domain (model, handler, service, repository) that serves both as a usable user-management starting point and the reference pattern for adding new domains; keep it or delete it, either way it shows the conventions.

nodes.label: context.Context propagation convention
nodes.rationale: Every stack layer (handler > service > repository) passes context.Context as the first argument for cancellation/deadline propagation; no global request state.

nodes.label: No global state / dependency injection
nodes.rationale: No global state; dependencies injected through constructors and function parameters so layers are testable in isolation.

nodes.label: Go internal/ package boundary
nodes.rationale: Prevents code outside the module from importing app packages; the Go equivalent of 'you don't know it's a library until you need it to be one'.

nodes.label: Repository pattern
nodes.rationale: Concrete structs (not interfaces by default) with sqlx for scanning; all SQL lives in repository methods and the service layer never constructs SQL. Use interfaces where testing requires stubs.

nodes.label: Single binary with subcommands
nodes.rationale: main.go calls cmd.Execute(); the HTTP server is just another subcommand (serve), mirroring Laravel artisan; running gobase with no args prints help.

nodes.label: Vertical slicing by feature
nodes.rationale: Each domain is a flat folder under internal/ containing all layers (model, handler, service, repository); adding a domain means one new folder, removing one means rm -rf internal/<domain>/. Infrastructure shared across domains stays as shared packages.

nodes.label: HTTP server infrastructure
nodes.rationale: internal/server owns chi router assembly (RequestID, request logging, recovery), graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM with 30s drain deadline, JSON response helpers, and http.Server timeouts.

nodes.label: golang-migrate migrations
nodes.rationale: SQL-file-based migrations with CLI integration and no ORM coupling; files embedded via //go:embed so the binary is self-contained.

nodes.label: Sentinel error mapping
nodes.rationale: Services define and return sentinel errors (ErrNotFound, ErrValidation, ErrConflict, ErrForbidden, ErrUnauthorized); server.codeFrom maps them with errors.Is to 404/422/409/403/401; unknown errors default to 500 and are logged at ERROR level.
